To sum up, we need to:
1. Add a new `payment-token` bot config param (for demo you will use this [repo](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibar) and this [token](https://gnosisscan.io/token/0x2b20faaf99d1f849815d55bed626bde050aa12c4)) 
2. Update pay.ubq.fi to accept the UBQ token
Correct?

Yes, as far as I remember assignees shouldn't get incentives for commenting, but [this](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/780) is a different case.
We have 3 parties who get rewards:
1. Issue assignee
2. Issue creator
3. Issue commenters
In [this](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/780) particular case issue assignee and issue creator are the same that is why we need to consolidate the reward (issue creator reward + issue solver reward) and generate a permit with a unique nonce (across a single issue) so that other parties (i.e. issue commenters) could also get their rewards.
This "reward consolidation" feature appeared in an effort to find a way to generate unique nonces for commenters. Perhaps we could generate nonces this way:
1. Issue assignee: `keccak256(issue.node_id . bountyHunter.node_id . "ISSUE_ASSIGNEE")`
2. Issue creator: `keccak256(issue.node_id . bountyHunter.node_id . "ISSUE_CREATOR")`
3. Issue commenter: `keccak256(issue.node_id . bountyHunter.node_id . "ISSUE_COMMENTER")`
So right now there are no any blockers for implementing the "consolidation feature", right?

### Context
Check this [issue](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/780)
There are 2 permits generated:
1. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/780#issuecomment-1696422095 (issue solver reward)
2. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/780#issuecomment-1696422165 (issue creator reward)
Right now we use `issue.node_id` as a permit nonce so those 2 permits are using the same nonce. It means that only 1 of those permits is claimable.
We should change the logic of how permit nonce is generated so that the permit (bounty reward + comment incentives) could be claimed by different bounty hunters in a single issue. 
Perhaps we could generate nonce smth like `keccak256(issue.node_id . bountyHunter.user_id)`.
### Tasks
1. Consolidate the permits based on contributor (right now there can be multiple posted for a single contributor.)
    - When combined, the caption should list out all of the reasons. e.g. "Issue creator, and assignee rewards: "
2. Use the issue ID and user ID for the nonce. 
    - This enforces that a contributor can only get paid out one time per issue.
